extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, policymakers, oversight committees, and DoD/Army officials
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of the Walter Reed (WRAMC) OMB Circular A-76 public-private competition, its procedural compliance, oversight issues, cost comparisons, and workforce impacts. Focused on how A-76 studies should be conducted, documented, and reviewed in the military/DoD context.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 time limits for competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The new circular established new deadlines for the completion of A-76 studies - 12 months for standard competitions, and 90 days for streamlined competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD multi-function A-76 studies were otherwise limited by law to 30 months (and DoD rules limit to 48 months); competitions that exceed established deadlines should be cancelled or require timely OMB waivers/approved extensions. Excessive length increases costs and undermines productivity and savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OMB waivers and use of prior Circular rules
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD may use pre-2003 Circular rules only under an OMB waiver limited to timely completion or cancellation of the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DoD Competitive Sourcing Official is responsible for ensuring the prior Circular is used only to achieve timely completion; if the waiver's completion date passes and no approved extension was requested, the initiative should have been cancelled rather than continued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of competitive sourcing officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies were required to appoint competitive sourcing officials, such as the Human Resource Advisor (HRA), Agency Tender Official (ATO), Performance Work Statement (PWS) Team Leader; Source Selection Authority (SSA); Contracting Officer (CO), and Competitive Sourcing Official (CSO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These roles are mandatory for conducting the A-76 process and each has specific responsibilities in developing the PWS, certification, source selection, and protests/appeals handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) clarity and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS describes the work to be performed under the competition and includes all responsibilities and requirements; performance standards, acceptable deviations from the standards, and how the contract will be monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IRO provides an analysis of the PWS for clarity and completeness; the PWS is critical as it provides the baseline for all cost estimates and comparisons between the MEO and contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Review Official (IRO)/Army Audit Agency (AAA) certification and reconstructibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRO/AAA independently reviews and certifies the MEO’s bid proposal; the certification must be based on a reconstructible record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAA actions (e.g., withdrawing certification because it could not reconstruct the basis to certify the MEO) undermine the process; certification should be fully documented so others can reconstruct the basis of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and transparency of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must accurately compare the government MEO’s evaluated proposed price and the contractor’s evaluated proposed price using the PWS baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recalculations and changes to solicitations must be documented; transition and administrative costs (e.g., MEDCOM costs, VERA/VSIP, severance, civilian personnel administration) should be included when assessing net savings so reported ‘annual savings’ reflect full costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on solicitation amendments and stability of solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive amendments to the solicitation (e.g., the Army revised the solicitation 16 times resulting in about 1,500 changes) alter workload and can decertify in-house bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant, numerous post-issuance changes to a solicitation can invalidate or destabilize the competition; solicitations should be stable and workload data current to ensure fair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of current and accurate workload data
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions must use workload data that reflect current operational realities (the WRAMC competition used dated workload and expectations created before GWOT, while workload had grown significantly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to account for changed workloads (e.g., surge in wounded warriors after combat operations began) results in understaffing and misestimation of required personnel and costs; workload assumptions should be updated before final cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory notification and implementation requirements for personnel actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army had to give Congress at least 45 days notice of the pending reduction-in-force (RIF), and give WRAMC employees at least 60 days notice of a pending RIF (10 U.S.C. 1597(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory timing and notification requirements must be observed prior to implementing workforce reductions or contractor transitions; these are mandatory legal prerequisites to implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with appropriations and the Antideficiency Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines and conduct of A-76 studies are constrained by Defense Appropriations language (e.g., prohibitions on conducting studies beyond specified time limits) and spending must comply with the Antideficiency Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing a competition in apparent violation of appropriation limits or without respecting the Antideficiency Act raises legal problems; Congress takes such violations seriously and they can trigger oversight or intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely resolution and management of protests and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions are subject to GAO protests and AAA appeals; the number and handling of appeals/protests can materially delay completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests and appeals should be handled promptly and with proper documentation; protracted protest cycles contribute to cost increases and workforce instability and can necessitate reconsideration or cancellation of the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of workforce impacts (retention, recruitment, morale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcing a pending A-76 competition often causes skilled personnel to quit and raises anxiety, adversely affecting recruitment and retention; prolonged competitions exacerbate morale problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision makers should weigh destabilizing workforce effects — particularly when concurrent events (e.g., BRAC) exist — and consider limiting scope (e.g., avoiding privatizing clinical workforce) or cancelling studies when negative personnel impacts outweigh benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to estimate and include transition costs in savings analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition costs (e.g., VERA/VSIP, severance pay, civilian personnel administration, MEDCOM administration) should be estimated and included when calculating the net savings of privatization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported annual savings should be net of transition and organizational costs; extraordinary expenses from prolonged competitions can reduce or eliminate estimated savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of BRAC and other concurrent policy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: BRAC decisions (e.g., realignment and planned closing of Walter Reed campus) affect staffing, capital investments, and decisions on privatization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When facilities face BRAC actions, funding commitments for infrastructure may be withheld and privatization decisions should account for BRAC-related uncertainty; combining BRAC and A-76 can compound workforce destabilization and operational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and oversight for cancellation or regulatory relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRG recommended the Secretary of Defense provide service secretaries the opportunity to apply for regulatory relief from future A-76 studies for WRAMC and other military medical treatment facilities only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory relief or cancellation is an available remedy when A-76 studies prove destabilizing or impractical; oversight bodies should consider exemptions for sensitive facility types where appropriate.
